doc.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

title: Sidney Bechet, church influence and Herlin Riley
summary: The church shapes the music; Herlin Riley will not play 'Saints' outside church.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Yeah. When you were talking about the force of the trumpet players and the drummers.
It made me think of Sidney Bechet, who is like with that soprano sax like a laser.
And his vibrato. You notice how his vibrato is church-like? Like, oh come on the Gospel singer, the famous Gospel singer.

Yes. Has that power. And it’s the same thing, the church informed the music quite a bit. You know Herlin Riley to this day, his father was a minister, sorry, his grandfather was a minister and so was his grandmother. He won’t play “When the Saints Go Marching In” if it’s not in church. You know it’s like that’s sacred music and this is a secular venue, we’re not going to do that. So I’ve seen him at festivals and the band leader calls “Saints” and he would just lay out. You know?
Do a Chuck Berry on him.
Oh yeah. I thought I told you not to mention that.
